article_title: People all saying same thing as photo of cop at airport goes viral
article_content:
An image showing a law‑enforcement officer standing inside Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport has gone viral on social media, as airports across the U.S. grapple with staff shortages linked to the ongoing partial government shutdown.
The photo, which shows an armed officer positioned near airport operations while long lines are visible outside, has been widely shared on X and Threads amid growing scrutiny of the federal government’s decision to deploy law‑enforcement personnel to assist at airports as Transportation Security Administration (TSA) workers continue to work without pay.
The image was first shared on Threads by user and American political strategist @adamparkhomenko with the caption “What a shot,” and later reposted on X by The Tennessee Holler, where it has attracted over 520,000 views.
Comments accompanying the image focused on visible congestion outside the terminal and questioned the role of law‑enforcement officers inside airports during the shutdown.
One reply under the post read: “$50 per hour vs TSA $25 per hour—the view from the window,” referring to widely shared claims about pay disparities between TSA officers and other federal agents.
Why the Photo Is Drawing Attention
The viral image comes as airports nationwide experience severe delays following weeks of staffing disruptions at the TSA, which is overseen by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
Funding for DHS expired on February 14 after lawmakers failed to reach an agreement over immigration enforcement policy, triggering a partial government shutdown.
Because TSA officers are classified as essential workers, they are required to continue screening passengers and baggage despite not receiving pay during the shutdown. DHS has said more than 400 TSA employees have quit since the funding lapse began, citing financial strain related to rent, food, childcare and commuting costs.
In response to mounting call‑outs and resignations, the Trump administration began deploying agents from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to assist at airports starting Monday.
Lauren Bis, acting assistant secretary for public affairs at DHS, told Newsweek earlier this week that the administration was taking action to reduce disruptions.
“President Trump is taking action to deploy hundreds of ICE officers, that are currently funded by Congress, to airports being adversely impacted,” Bis said. “This will help bolster TSA efforts to keep our skies safe and minimize air travel disruptions.”
Bis added that DHS would not confirm the specific locations where ICE agents are operating “for operational security reasons.”
ICE agents have been deployed to several major airports, including those serving Atlanta, New York, New Jersey, Philadelphia, Chicago, New Orleans, Houston and Phoenix.
Public Reaction
The presence of law‑enforcement officers at airports has sparked debate, with some social media users questioning how the deployments help alleviate long security lines.
Others contrasted the situation with TSA officers continuing to work without pay, a dynamic that has fueled broader criticism of how the shutdown is affecting frontline airport staff.
The latest shutdown is the third in less than six months to force TSA agents to work unpaid, raising concerns among airlines and industry groups about the long‑term impact on airport operations. Executives from major carriers, including Delta Air Lines, have urged lawmakers to restore DHS funding, warning that delays and disruptions could worsen if the standoff continues.
